checks.invariant: A deterministically refused embed batch must not stop the embed step for rows of other principals: the loop should split, skip or quarantine the refused rows and keep advancing, as the render stage does (_land row-by-row retry then 'failed' quarantine, backend.py:1298-1321).
checks.result: _embed_step sets last=0 on every run (backend.py:1442), selects the lowest-id 'embedding IS NULL' rows (embed.py:172-182), and on any page with a failed batch records stopped_by and breaks the whole loop (backend.py:1466-1468). embed_page lands the batches that answered (gather return_exceptions, embed.py:319-325) but never splits the refused batch, never marks its rows, and _embed_with_retry retries only when a Retry-After header exists (embed.py:346-368). No per-row embed state exists, so the same rows reform the same first batch on every run. Unlike the render stage, there is no quarantine.

checks.invariant: Batches sent to the shipped OpenAI provider must stay under its declared hard caps (300000 tokens per request, 8192 per input), whatever script the content is in.
checks.result: token_batched meters each row by provider.estimate_tokens. For OpenAI that is ceil(len/4) (openai.py:63-64, provider.py:94-96), against 5/6 of 300000, which is 250000 estimated tokens (embed.py:61,121,333-335). The real count only has to be about 1.2 times the estimate to break the cap: about 3.3 chars per token or denser. CJK, Cyrillic, emoji and symbol-heavy text are all that dense or denser, so the batch is refused. Per input: chunks are at most 2048 chars (chunking.py:217), which is at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes, so byte-level BPE cannot exceed MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=8192. truncated_for (embed.py:136-144) is a no-op there, and a per-input refusal is not reachable through default chunking. LangChain declares no caps (langchain.py:34-36), so vfs predicts no refusal for it; model2vec and other local providers do not refuse.

checks.invariant: Bounded local proof: after principal alice writes token-dense ordinary text, bob's later writes still get vectors after repeated reindex runs.
checks.result: DatabaseStorage on SQLite with a fake provider. It declares the shipped OpenAI caps (8192/2048/300000) and estimates with vfs's estimate_tokens, but enforces the caps with 1 token per CJK char. A cap overrun raises a 400-shaped error with no Retry-After. EMBED_PAGE_ROWS=4096 was left unscaled. FULL: alice (read_write on /alice) writes 4096 files of 160 CJK chars each (estimate 40, real 156), about 2 MB in total; bob then writes 50 English files. In all 3 reindex runs every batch was refused ([2048 inputs, 81920 estimated, 319488 real]). Bob's chunks stayed embedded 1/51 (only the pre-existing README), and unembedded stayed 4146 each run. reindex returned success=True with one retryable 'vfs.unavailable' warning: 'embedding stopped after 0 requests: BadRequest: Requested 319488 tokens, max 300000 tokens per request'. Bob's glean vector leg hits=2, against hits=52 in the CONTROL run without alice, where bob was 51/51 embedded after run 1. PARTIAL (only max_batch_tokens scaled to 3000): alice writes 10 CJK files of 300 chars. The refused first batch (48 rows: alice's 10 plus 38 of bob's) stayed NULL in all 3 runs; bob ended at 63/101 embedded and the vector leg at hits=64. Each FULL run took about 4 s wall time.

checks.invariant: Harness source for the local check (fake capped provider, principals, scenarios, scaling notes).
checks.result: The harness used for the control, partial and full scenarios. It uses no network, makes no hosted provider call, and produces hash vectors.

candidates.title: One refused embed batch at the head of the NULL-embedding keyset stops vector indexing for every later writer on the store
candidates.description: The reindex embed step always restarts at chunk id 0. It takes the lowest-id unembedded rows, cuts them into batches using a ceil(len/4) token estimate, and stops the whole step at the first page where any batch fails. A batch the provider refuses deterministically has no split, skip or per-row quarantine. Its rows stay NULL and form the same first batch on every later run. With the shipped OpenAI provider, ordinary text denser than about 3.3 chars per token (CJK, Cyrillic, emoji) exceeds the real 300000-token request cap while staying under the 250000 estimated budget. A principal with write access to any path on the mount can write about 4096 small CJK files (about 2 MB). After that, every chunk any principal writes later never gets a vector, across any number of reindex runs, and glean's vector leg misses all of it. A smaller amount of such text permanently leaves the neighbouring rows that share its batch (other principals' content) unembedded, and slows the rest to one page per run.
candidates.root_cause: _embed_step (backend.py:1416-1483) treats every provider failure as transient: it records stopped_by and breaks the loop (backend.py:1466-1468), and the next run restarts at last=0 (backend.py:1442). embed_page/_embed_with_retry (embed.py:266-355) do not tell a deterministic refusal apart from a transient one, never bisect a refused batch, and keep no per-row failed state, so select_unembedded (embed.py:172-182) returns the same poison rows first on every run. token_batched (embed.py:112-133) meters with the OpenAI adapter's ceil(len/4) estimate (openai.py:63-64, provider.py:94-96), which undercounts token-dense scripts. Rows the writer controls can therefore push a batch past the hard cap the adapter itself declares (openai.py:34).
candidates.intended_behavior: Batches should be metered by a bound that cannot undercount, such as UTF-8 bytes for byte-level BPE. A refused batch without Retry-After should be bisected down to single rows, and a single row still refused should be quarantined with a per-row failed state that select_unembedded skips and the report counts. This mirrors the render stage's _land (backend.py:1298-1321). The loop should then keep advancing to later pages, so one writer's content cannot stop vector indexing for other principals.

trace.description: Principal alice, with read_write on /alice only, writes ordinary CJK text files. No content, script or length rule applies beyond the write gate.
reindex chunks the bodies into rows of at most 2048 chars. Alice's rows get lower chunk ids than anything written later.
Every run starts the keyset at last=0.
The page is the lowest-id 'embedding IS NULL' rows, so alice's rows come first on every run.
Cost is provider.estimate_tokens = ceil(len/4), metered against 250000 (5/6 of 300000). A 2048-input batch of 160-char CJK rows estimates at 81920 tokens but is really about 319488.
The provider refuses with a 400 that carries no Retry-After, and the error is re-raised with no split and no row marking.
gather(return_exceptions) keeps the first failure. The refused batch's rows land nothing.
outcome.failure records stopped_by and breaks, so later pages are never selected. The same rows head the next run, and every later principal's chunks stay embedding NULL indefinitely.

evidence.description: Any provider failure on a page breaks the whole embed loop.
last = 0 on every run, so the poison rows are always re-selected first.
The sibling render stage retries row by row and quarantines a refused row as 'failed'. The embed step has no equivalent.
The batch budget is 5/6 of max_batch_tokens, metered by the provider's estimate.
The shipped adapter declares MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=300000 and uses estimate_tokens (line 63-64).
Only an exception carrying Retry-After is retried; a 400 refusal is not split or marked.
The operator sees only a retryable 'unavailable' warning naming no rows, while reindex reports success=True.

conditions.description: The mount is configured with an embedder whose hard caps are enforced on real tokens while vfs meters them with ceil(len/4). The shipped OpenAIEmbeddingProvider is the one shipped adapter that declares such caps. LangChain declares none, and local providers (model2vec, hashing) do not refuse.
The writer needs write access to some path on the same DatabaseStorage mount. No other right is needed, and reindex is run by the operator as usual.

The writer's token-dense rows must have lower chunk ids than the victims' unembedded rows, that is, be written before them or still be unembedded. A full stop needs about 4096 such rows (one EMBED_PAGE_ROWS page) with real tokens above about 147 per row. Fewer rows permanently strand only the rows that share their batch, and throttle the rest to one page per run.

OpenAI's tokenizer must count the text at more than about 1.2 times len/4, and must refuse a request over 300000 tokens deterministically, with a 400 and no Retry-After. The repository declares the cap. CJK at about 1 token per character in cl100k is widely documented, but it was not measured here: the provider was a local fake.

execution.attacker_perspective: An agent or user (alice) with read_write on its own subtree of a shared DatabaseStorage mount that is backed by the OpenAI embedder, whose victims (bob) write content later.
payloads: 4096 files /alice/notes/NNNNN.txt, each a distinct 160-character run of CJK ideographs from U+4E00 (estimate 40 tokens, real 156)
PARTIAL variant: 10 files of 300 CJK chars with max_batch_tokens scaled to 3000
instructions: Mount DatabaseStorage(url=sqlite+aiosqlite:///scratch<tmp>/full.db, embedder=CappedProvider) with a fake provider. It declares max_input_tokens=8192, max_batch_inputs=2048 and max_batch_tokens=300000, estimates with vfs.embedding.estimate_tokens, counts 1 token per CJK char when enforcing the caps, and raises a 400-shaped error with empty headers on an overrun.
As system, create /alice and /bob, grant alice and bob read_write on their own directories, and reindex once.
As alice, write the 4096 CJK files. As bob, write 50 ordinary English files.
Run reindex three times. After each run, count embedded and NULL chunk rows per principal. Then run glean as bob and read legs['vector'].
Control: the same run with zero alice files.
execution.observed_result: FULL, with caps and page size unscaled: in each of 3 runs, 2 requests were refused ([2048 inputs, 81920 estimated, 319488 real]). Bob stayed at 1 of 51 chunks embedded and unembedded=4146 every run. reindex returned success=True with the warning 'Unavailable: embedding stopped after 0 requests: BadRequest: Requested 319488 tokens, max 300000 tokens per request' (retryable=True). Bob's glean vector leg had hits=2. CONTROL: bob had 51 of 51 embedded after run 1, and the vector leg had hits=52. PARTIAL: the same 48-row first batch (alice's 10 plus 38 of bob's) was refused in all 3 runs, leaving bob at 63 of 101 embedded and the vector leg at hits=64.

remediation.strategy: Meter with a bound that cannot undercount, and stop treating a deterministic refusal as a reason to end the run. (1) The OpenAI adapter's estimate_tokens should return the UTF-8 byte length: byte-level BPE never yields more tokens than bytes, so batches and truncation stay under the hard caps. (2) In embed_page, a refused batch without Retry-After should be bisected recursively, and a single row that is still refused should be returned as a per-row failure. (3) Those rows should get a quarantine stamp: an embed_failed column or a sentinel state that select_unembedded and count_unembedded exclude, reset when the chunk's content_hash changes, with the count reported in the embedding extra. (4) _embed_step should break only on transient failures (timeout, 429/Retry-After, network) and otherwise keep advancing 'last'. Regression test: a fake provider counting 1 token per CJK char and enforcing 300000 per request; alice writes 4096 CJK files and bob writes 50; after one reindex, all of bob's chunks are embedded and alice's are either embedded or counted as quarantined.

likelihood.reason: The attacker cost is low: one ordinary write of about 2 MB of CJK text by any principal with write access to some path, and no special rights. It needs the OpenAI embedder (the only shipped adapter with hard caps) and token-dense content. Benign CJK or Cyrillic corpora with default 2048-char chunks trigger the same refusal (about 488 chunks per batch, about 1M chars, well over 300000 real tokens), so it will also happen without malice.

impact.reason: The effect is persistent and store-wide: no chunk written later by any principal gets a vector, across every reindex, until an operator finds and deletes the poison rows or changes the provider. glean's vector leg silently misses that content, though the lexical leg still finds it, and nothing is disclosed. Each run also spends refused provider requests. The report names no rows, and its retryable=True flag invites endless retries.

confidence.reason: The vfs logic (no split, skip or quarantine; break; restart at 0) is source-visible and was demonstrated with unscaled caps and page size. The external fact, OpenAI's real tokenizer counts and its 400 on going over 300000, comes from the repo's declared caps and public tokenizer behaviour, not from a live measurement.

hardening: The embed warning's 'stopped after N requests' counts only successful requests (report.requests is incremented after success, embed.py:305), so a run whose every batch is refused reports 'after 0 requests' while the provider received and refused several.

A deterministic 400 refusal is classified retryable=True ErrorKind.unavailable (backend.py:1475-1482), which tells an operator to retry a run that will fail identically forever; deterministic refusals should be classified separately and name the refused chunk ids or paths.

truncated_for (embed.py:136-144) shares the ceil(len/4) estimator. It is safe today only because chunks are capped at 2048 chars (at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes, so at most 8192 byte-level tokens). Raising chunk_size or adding a prefix would let one row exceed MAX_INPUT_TOKENS=8192 and hit the same head-of-line stop through the per-input cap.
